question: In the context of the Indian banking system, the ‘Cash Reserve Ratio’ is decided by _____.
solution:
The correct answer is__** the Reserve Bank of India.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Every commercial bank** in India is required by the** RBI **to keep a** specific minimum amount of deposits** as a** reserve**, which is known as the "**cash reserve ratio" (CRR).**
 
• The CRR shall be set in accordance with **RBI guidelines.**
 
• Cash Reserve Ratio ensures that a** part of the bank’s deposit is with the Central Bank **and is hence, **secure.**
 
• **Controlling inflation** is one of CRR's other goals.
 
• When there is **significant economic inflation**, the **RBI increases the CRR **to l**ower the amount of cash available** to banks for **loan approvals.**
 
• It restricts the **economy's ability to move money**, which** lowers investments and inflation.**
 
• As per the current monetary policy announced on September 30, 2022:
 
 
• The repo rate stands at 4.00% and the reverse repo rate at 3.35%.
 
• The marginal standing facility (MSF) rate and the Bank Rate stand at 4.25%.
 
• **The CRR rate and SLR rate stand at 4.50% and 18.00%.**
